messages.subject: Re: three variables tvecm
parts:
Hi Davide

This is a question that comes quite often, so I wrote a answer to it
on the FAQ: https://github.com/MatthieuStigler/tsDyn/wiki/FAQ
Please have a look, and in case a clarification/further question is
needed, don't hesitate to ask back on this list!

Best

Matthieu


On May 31, 12:33 pm, davidereat...@gmail.com wrote:
> Dear Matthieu Stigler,
>
>  I am a student in University of Padua Statistics' department, and I am
> working on my master thesis with R. I am analyzing the relathionship
> between three I(1) cointegrated variables. These variables are: electricity
> prices (Pel), exchange rate (Tc) and oil prices (Pp). Parametric test for
> Granger causality (based on VAR rappresentation of differentiated
> variables) doesn't report presence of causality. But if I implement Diks
> and Panchenko non parametric test for Granger causality I detect some
> causality between Pel and Tc. Moreover Hansen and Seo (2002) test for
> linear cointegration detects doubts about the linear cointegration hypothesis
> (p-value 0.02). So these signals of non-linearity lead me to TVECM representation.
> But how can I analyse these three variables jointly with a TVECM representation?
> I try to estimate bivariate TVECM with Pel and Tc and it highlights short
> run relationship that linear VECM doesn't highlight.So I think this can be
> a right approach for the problem but my goal is to consider all the three
> variables.
> Kind regards,
> Davide
